title: Phoenix softlaunch provisioning notes
content:
Purpose:

This doc captures the capacity and operational plan for a controlled soft-launch ("Phoenix" codename) of a new mid-sized decoder model variant. Target audience: infra on-call, rollout owner, serving runtime, and SREs. This is intentionally pragmatic — contains conservative headroom numbers, warmup approach, and contingency triggers.

Quick summary and ask:
- Softlaunch window: 3 weeks starting 2026-03-10 (can shift based on infra readiness).
- Initial traffic steering: start at 0.5% global traffic, ramp to 5% over 6 days if metrics OK, then hold for 2 weeks for quality and KV footprint observation.
- Request: reserve one full GPU pod per region for coordinated warmup + 10% global headroom on top of baseline capacity for the first two weeks.

Model profile (Phoenix):
- Architecture: 34B dense decoder (production variant uses quantized kernels).
- Typical seq lengths: avg request tokens = 120, avg generated = 80, p95 request length = 420.
- KV cache density: measured on offline samples => approx 88 bytes per token stored in KV (post-serialization, compressed).
- Per-request KV working set (typical): ~200 tokens \u00d7 88 bytes = ~17.6 KB. P95 working set ~500 tokens => ~44 KB.

Estimate assumptions and conservative factors applied:
- Concurrency: baseline region concurrency at 95th percentile preserved. We assume Phoenix traffic will have slightly higher long-tail (p95 length) so apply a 1.25x multiplier on memory and IO for worst-case headroom in first 14 days.
- Warmup inefficiency: first 48h of rollout may have elevated KV misses and cold KV activity; count an additional 30% transient KV bandwidth increase in that window.
- GPU memory: quantized model resident memory ~68 GB GPU RAM when loaded with standard shard layout. We plan for one additional model replica per region (for warmup/prefix seeding) and prefer colocated NVMe cache on node where possible.

Regional capacity sketch (per major region):
- us-west1 (primary): baseline serving pods (Phoenix-compatible) = 24 pods.
  - Extra reserve: +3 pods for warmup (12% headroom).
  - KV bandwidth: baseline peak 420 MB/s, projected incremental for 5% traffic = +21 MB/s, add warmup transient +30% => +27 MB/s.
- us-east4: baseline pods = 18, reserve +2 pods.
- eu-west1: baseline pods = 14, reserve +2 pods.
- ap-south1 (limited): baseline pods = 8, reserve +1 pod.
Notes: reserves are sized to allow regional routing to absorb spike without cross-region failovers for the first two weeks. If reserves are not available, route softlaunch traffic to subset of regions (us-west1 + us-east4 only) and mark others as dark.

KV cache footprint and storage impact (global, rough):
- Active user-set for softlaunch (at 5%): ~3.6M daily active sessions across customers (derived from global 72M DAU baseline).
- Assumed average concurrent KV residency window per session: 18 hours (warm conversations).
- Working set per active session (avg): 17.6 KB -> total live KV ~63 GB per million concurrent sessions.
- For 3.6M sessions (scaled across time windows), expected steady-state KV layer increase ~226 GB.
- Add 25% buffer for serialization overhead + index structures => plan for 300 GB of additional KV storage globally in the first month. This fits comfortably on existing distributed KV clusters in all regions, but watch index IOPS.

Performance and cost impacts (high-level):
- Token-level CPU/GPU overhead: continuous batching benefits will amortize cost; expect incremental per-token inference cost delta ~+8% (empirical estimate from dev perf runs).
- Network inter-region egress: if we cannot reserve regional capacity and must steer traffic cross-region, worst-case egress ~120 MB/s sustained for warmup windows (expect cost and higher latency).

Operational warmup plan (minimum viable):
1) Stage 0 (pre-softlaunch, during next 10 days):
   - Bake the quantized kernel set in images; run integration perf smoke in canary cluster and confirm p95 latency within SLO on simulated 1% traffic.
   - Ensure KMS keys and model artifacts are staged in each region's artifact repo.
   - Create route config in API gateway with initial weight 0.5%.
2) Stage 1 (softlaunch day 0-2):
   - Enable 0.5% weight across target regions.
   - Kick off coordinated prefix-warmup job that replays a representative 100k prompt corpus per region to prefill KV for expected user prefixes. The replay jobs should be rate-limited to avoid saturating KV IOPS (start at 60 req/s per warmup pod).
   - Monitor KV miss-rate, KV bandwidth, GPU memory pressure, and p95 latency every 5 minutes.
3) Stage 2 (ramp days 3-8):
   - Conditional ramp to 5% over 6 days: double weight every 48 hours if all four KPIs stable (latency within target, error rate <0.2%, KV miss-rate plateauing, regional CPU/GPU <75% utilization).
4) Stage 3 (holds and observation days 9-21):
   - Hold at target weight (5%) for at least 14 days for data collection.
   - Run nightly KV compact jobs and collect delta telemetry.

KPIs to gate ramp decisions (measured per-region):
- 95th percentile token latency (inference) — must be <= baseline p95 + 15%
- Request error rate (5xx/timeout) <= baseline + 0.2% absolute
- KV miss-rate trending down or stable (no >10% sustained increase)
- Region GPU utilization should not exceed 85% sustained (5m avg)

Contingency and rollback triggers (automated where possible):
- Auto-rollback to previous default model if region p95 latency exceeds threshold for 10m and sustained for 3 samples.
- If KV IOPS > 80% node capacity for >10m, throttle softlaunch traffic by 50% and run targeted prefix eviction for low-value keys.
- If cross-region egress spikes above planned budget (one-time threshold in CloudSpend alert), immediately cap traffic to 2% and open an incident.

Notes for SRE/on-call runbook:
- Alerts to wire to #infra-phoenix channel: INFRA-PHOENIX-LATENCY, INFRA-PHOENIX-ERRORS, INFRA-PHOENIX-KV-IOPS.
- Runtime commands: script to reduce Phoenix weight to 0.5%: infra/traffic-ctl set-weight phoenix 0.5 (documented in runbook).
- How to drain warmup pods: infra/ops/drain-pod --model phoenix --region <region> --grace 60s.

Open questions and risks (needs input):
- Is 1 additional replica per region (reserve) acceptable from cost perspective for customers on Dedicated clusters? / finance input needed.
- We assume KV index growth linear with sessions; need back-of-envelope validation against actual index samples from prod KV (ask data infra).
- Fallback model variant: we should publish recommended fallback to a 13B family variant in route config to reduce cost during rollbacks.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Confirm reserve pod availability in eu-west1 and ap-south1 (Ethan, 2026-02-18)
- Run larger synthetic warmup run (1M prompts) in staging to validate KV serialization sizes (Maya, 2026-02-22)
- Provide cost delta estimate for reserved pods across 4 regions for finance review (Jules, 2026-02-20)

Appendix (short calc notes):
- KV per-token 88 bytes measured from local serialization bench.
- Average working set per session = 17.6 KB => 63 GB per 1M concurrent sessions.
- Expected additional global KV storage at 5% traffic ~226 GB -> plan 300 GB buffer for operational safety.

If you have immediate blockers, raise in #infra-phoenix. Otherwise I will publish a 1-page TL;DR to the softlaunch ticket and coordinate with product rollout owner next week.

Ravi
Infra Capacity (owner)
